create_nuclearindustry.ponder.accelerato: A particle accelerator starts at its controller. The beam leaves it on the face opposite its panel.
Right in front of it goes the Ion Source, with its shaft across the beam. It turns hydrogen into protons: fill it by pipe.
From the source the beamline runs on. Each RF Cavity adds energy: a longer linac with more cavities reaches higher energies.
Quadrupole Magnets keep the beam focused. Put one at least every four blocks, or most of the beam is lost on the walls.
The line ends in a Beam Dump or a target. The dump soaks up the whole beam, and becomes radioactive doing it.
Klystrons, Magnet Power Supplies and Vacuum Pumps beside the line power it, from a shaft or with Forge Energy.
Right-click the controller to open its panel and start the beam. It glows through the windows of the Beam Pipes.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.centrifuge: The Centrifuge separates uranium hexafluoride by enrichment. It turns through its back, at 32 RPM or more.
Pipe UF6 into the top or the sides.
The enriched product leaves through the front...
...and the depleted tails through the bottom.
Chain centrifuges into a cascade: natural to LEU, LEU to HEU, HEU to weapons grade. Pipe each stage's tails back into the stage before it.
It also separates Lithium-6 from lithium.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.civil_defe: Blast Doors
A blast door is a rectangle of steel or lead Blast Door leaves, 2x2 to 4x4, with a ring of Blast Door Frame around it.
One block of the ring is the Blast Door Controller. Its shaft runs through the wall, across the door.
A rising redstone signal opens it: the panel slides sideways into the wall, towards the controller...
...and a falling one shuts it. A shaft turning one way opens it and the other way shuts it, faster the faster it turns.
Shut, it holds back blast waves and radiation; open, the doorway lets both through. A comparator reads how far open it is.
If a leaf or a frame block is broken, the door slams shut.
Fallout Shelters
A Shelter Filtration Unit certifies the sealed room it stands in as a shelter.
Every wall block the air touches must hold back blasts and radiation well enough: glass will not do. Goggles on the unit name the weakest wall.
Inside a certified shelter a blast wave keeps only a tenth of its force. A shut blast door counts as wall.
While the unit turns at 16 RPM or more it filters the air: fallout and contaminated ground give those inside a twentieth of their dose.
A Seismic Detector feels every nuclear detonation in its dimension. Goggles show the distance, bearing and strength of the last eight.
A comparator reads it: the signal jumps with a blast and fades back to 0 over five minutes.
Sirens
The Air Raid Siren sounds a steady alert while it gets a redstone signal.
Without redstone it watches the sky: a missile, a bomb or a launch countdown aimed within 96 blocks of it, plus its fallout's reach, sets off the faster attack warning.
Goggles on it tell how long until the impact. It is heard up to 128 blocks away.
The Hand-Crank Siren has no power of its own: it sounds while the shaft under it turns at 32 RPM or more...
...and wails higher the faster it turns. A comparator reads 15 from it while it sounds.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.containmen: A Containment Door is the way into a containment. Shut, it seals like the wall around it and holds 8 bar.
Click it or give it a redstone signal: it pulls out of its frame and slides sideways along the wall.
Open, the doorway is a hole: the containment is no longer sealed until the door shuts again.
While the containment behind it is more than 0.2 bar above the outside, the door is pressure-locked: neither a click nor redstone opens it.
Two doors side by side, hinged on opposite sides, open together and slide apart.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.control_ro: The Control Room
A control room runs a whole plant from one place. This one is laid out like a real plant's: tall instrument boards on the back wall, and the operators' desks set back in front of them.
Control Tables have a flat top, level with a desk's rail: here, the shift supervisor's at the back. Tables apart from the desks make a console of their own.
Look at a module or a console to see its card on the right of the screen: what it is set to, what it shows, where its redstone goes and what the console is linked to.
Every device starts unlinked. Click any block of a machine with the Control Room Linker, then click the device: reactors, steam generators, containments, turbines, cooling towers and tokamaks.
Linked to any other block, a device watches the radiation there. Devices reach 128 blocks; sneak-click one with the linker to unlink it.
Desks, tables and wall panels touching side by side, and wall panels above one another, make one console with one link: link any block of it and the whole console follows.
So the whole back board is one console on the reactor. Wall Control Panels hang on the face of a solid block and hold four modules upright.
Monitors side by side join into one screen of up to 8x8. A big screen lists the machine's readings beside a two-minute graph; a lone monitor shows one big reading per page.
Click a screen to change page, and wrench it to choose its title, layout, style, rows and up to three graph lines. A comparator reads its main value.
Control Desks join side by side and turn corners like stairs, so a console can wrap round its operators. A corner desk holds one module on each arm.
Consoles on different walls are separate: this one runs the tokamak. Each monitor screen links on its own, here to the tokamak and to a turbine, each in a style of its own.
Instruments and Screens
LED Displays show a reading in digits with its unit. In a row they join into one wider display of up to eight modules, set up by the leftmost: the wider, the more digits, with a label on top.
Chart Recorders draw up to three readings on paper. Feed them paper by hand or with a hopper, and wrench them to choose the pens and the speed.
Sneak-click one with an empty hand to tear the chart off as a Chart Roll, to read anywhere. A comparator reads the paper left.
Nuclear Alarms ring and power every side once their reading passes the threshold. Pick the reading on the top face and the threshold on the sides.
Too big a value reads OL; a reading the machine does not have reads dashes.
Bar Graphs show a reading as a column of twenty lights: green, amber in the 15%% under the alarm level and red from it. The alarm level is set in the module's screen.
Trend Recorders draw a reading over their last 48 samples, one every 1, 5 or 20 seconds.
The Core Map shows a fission core from above, north at the top: fuel green to red as it burns, control channels filling blue as their rods go in. Four in one block make one big map.
The Plasma Section is a cut through a tokamak: its plasma glows with the temperature, swells with the density and shakes as it grows unstable. Four in one block make one big screen too.
Annunciator Panels line the top of the board, six alarm windows each. Link a window with the linker, or the frame for all six, and wrench it to choose its alarm, threshold and label.
A window that trips flashes and the horn sounds until ACK; then it stays lit while the alarm lasts, flashes slowly once it clears and goes dark on RESET. The first to trip is marked first out.
Redstone pulses into its left and right sides press ACK and RESET. Its back and bottom give a signal while an alarm waits, and a comparator reads how many windows are lit.
Control Modules
Fit a control module by clicking a free slot with it. Straight desks, tables and wall panels hold four; a corner desk holds one on each arm.
Its lamp is green while it drives. Click it to raise the setpoint and sneak-click to lower it; its setup switches it to standby.
Indicator Lamps light on SCRAM, running, no signal, an open relief valve or any alarm. Gauges show one reading on a dial.
Wrench a module to set it up: its function, label, reading or alarm, and its redstone output. Functions the linked machine cannot use are greyed out.
Sneak-wrench a module to take just that module out. Sneak-wrench the block anywhere else to pick it up; its modules drop beside it.
Click a module with an empty hand to work it. The Push Button SCRAMs the reactor or resets the SCRAM, sends a pulse, or starts and shuts down a tokamak.
The Guarded Button keeps a SCRAM or a shutdown under a hinged cover: the first click lifts the cover, the second presses the button.
A sneaking click lets the cover down, and it falls shut by itself five seconds after the last click.
Levers switch the automatic SCRAM, the pressurizer heaters and spray, a tokamak's fuel, heating, start or shutdown, or a plain signal. The Key Switch turns a signal on and off.
Dials set the control rods' target, the automatic SCRAM threshold or a redstone level: click to turn one up, sneak-click to turn it down.
The Controller is an automatic operator: it holds reactor power or temperature through the rod target, primary pressure through the pressurizer, or a tokamak's fusion power.
Signals Out of the Room
Any module can put its state out as redstone, chosen in its setup: a lever or a lamp on or off, a button's pulse, a dial's level or a reading from 0 to 15.
Below the desk: out of the bottom and the back of the block it sits in.
On a Create Redstone Link frequency: pick its two items in the setup, and every receiver on that frequency within range puts the signal out.
Or on an Advanced Redstone Link code: four letters or digits instead of two items. Click the link to type its code; sneak-click it to switch between sending and receiving.

Control rods only move with pistons. Reactor Redstone Ports set to Insert rods or Withdraw rods light up until the rods reach the dialled target: wire them to the clutch and gearshift of the rod pistons.
A port in SCRAM mode lights when SCRAM is pressed or the automatic SCRAM trips: wire it to drive every rod in, whatever else the room is doing.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.cooling_to: A Cooling Tower stands on a full round floor of Cooling Tower Casing, 4 to 16 blocks in radius.
Ring by ring, the wall narrows to a waist about three quarters of the way up, then flares out again. The top stays open.
Its height may be from twice the radius plus 4 up to five times the radius. A bigger tower condenses more.
The Cooling Tower Controller goes in the bottom wall layer, centred on a side and facing out. Right-click it to form the tower.
Fluid Ports go in the floor or the two wall layers above it. One on INPUT takes steam or heavy steam...
...and one on OUTPUT gives back the same amount of water or heavy water.
Fans in the three bottom wall layers, facing out, add up to a quarter more each at 256 RPM, at most doubling the tower.
It condenses half its base radius times its height in mB/t, 24 here. A turbine with an Exhaust Port sends it its spent steam instead of condensing it, and makes twice the power.
A Cryogenic Plant liquefies helium for a tokamak's magnets. It is a 3x3 box of Cryogenic Plant Casing, 3 to 5 blocks tall; every layer adds capacity.
The Controller sits in a wall. Right-click it to form the plant.
Compressors in the walls take the rotation, at 128 RPM or more. They are hungry: about 10240 SU per RPM for each layer, shared between them.
A port on Warm Helium In takes back the helium the tokamak's coils boil off...
...and one on Liquid Helium Out sends it, cold, to the tokamak's Cryogenic Ports. A wrench changes a port's mode.
Each pass loses a little helium. The helium ash the plasma makes as it burns tops the loop up again.
The first helium comes from the air. With a port on Liquid Air Out the plant liquefies air instead, and a Centrifuge splits liquid air into liquid nitrogen and a trace of helium.
Liquid nitrogen poured into a Nitrogen In port precools the plant, which then makes half as much liquid helium again.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.electrolyz: The Electrolyzer uses rotation in place of electric current, at 32 RPM or more.
Fed water, it slowly concentrates heavy water. Heavy water then splits into deuterium gas.
It also reduces lithium carbonate to lithium metal.
Fluids leave through the front, items through the bottom.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.fan_acid_l: Acid Leaching is a fan treatment, like washing: an Encased Fan's air current takes it up passing through Sulfuric Acid.
A bucket places the acid as a source block. Wall it in at the sides so it does not run off.
Items on a depot, on a belt or flying in the air current past the acid are leached.
The acid dissolves what is worth keeping out of rock and sand. JEI lists every recipe of the treatment.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.fan_irradi: Irradiation is a fan treatment: an Encased Fan's air current takes it up passing a strongly radioactive block.
Use an Irradiation Source: its open cage lets the air through, where a full radioactive block would stop the current.
Items in the air current past it are irradiated: Thorium Dioxide breeds into Irradiated Thorium, the first step to uranium-233.
The block irradiates you too: shield it, and keep clear while it works.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.fuel_cycle: Uranium goes from the ground to a reactor in a line of Create machines. First, Crushing Wheels grind Raw Uranium into Crushed Raw Uranium.
Washing it with a fan through water gives Uranium Concentrate.
A Mechanical Mixer over a heated Basin leaches the concentrate with Sulfuric Acid into Yellowcake...
...and superheated, with hydrofluoric acid, turns yellowcake into uranium hexafluoride gas.
Centrifuges enrich the gas. Chain them into a cascade and pipe each stage's tails back to the stage before.
Mixed with water, the enriched gas gives Uranium Dioxide, and a Mechanical Press makes pellets of it.
Sequenced assembly on an iron sheet, two pellets and a press at a time, finishes the Uranium Reactor Fuel.
The Electrolyzer makes what fusion needs: heavy water and deuterium from water, lithium from lithium carbonate.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.fusion_pla: A turbine is a box of casing: 3 to 7 blocks wide and high, and 3 to 16 blocks long.
A column of rotors runs down its axis. Every rotor stage expands 20 mB/t of plasma steam.
Reinforced Turbine Glass can replace casing anywhere on a face, but not on edges or corners.
Fluid Ports go on the faces. One set to INPUT takes the plasma steam...
...and one set to OUTPUT returns the condensed water. Each pair passes 80 mB/t.
The Plasma Turbine sits at the centre of one end, its shaft pointing out. Right-click it to form the turbine.
Once formed, the rotor spins up while plasma steam flows, and the glass shows how full the turbine is.
Rotors and port pairs both cap the flow; the smaller limit wins. Longer turbines with more ports make more power.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_cont: The control room runs the plant from afar. Fit control modules into Control Desks and link them to the reactor with the Control Room Linker.
Containment Penetrations carry the pipes through the wall without unsealing it.
The weakest wall sets the limit: this window holds only 1.05 bar. If the pressure beats it, the wall bursts there and everything airborne escapes.
A Containment Monitor inside measures the sealed air: pressure, temperature, steam, hydrogen and airborne activity.
Overheated cladding gives off hydrogen. Above 4%% it may burn and above 8%% it always does: Recombiners remove it without a flame.
A Filtered Vent opened by redstone bleeds off the overpressure and lets out only 1%% of the airborne activity.
In a meltdown the fuel turns into Corium, which melts its way down...
...until a Core Catcher floor stops it: it spreads out and freezes into Solidified Corium, still radioactive but contained.
A dial set to Rod target chooses how deep the control rods should sit.

A Controller Module moves that target for you: on Automatic power or Automatic temperature it holds the power or the core temperature at its setpoint. On Automatic pressure it runs the pressurizer instead.
Rods only move with pistons. Redstone Ports set to Withdraw rods or Insert rods light up until the rods reach the target...
...so wire them to a Clutch and a Gearshift on the piston's shaft: the rods move while a port is lit, the way it asks.
A SCRAM button calls for full insertion and beats every other setting until it is reset.
Link each window of an Annunciator Panel to an alarm. It flashes fast with a horn until acknowledged, stays lit while the alarm lasts and flashes slowly once it clears.
A Chart Recorder draws up to three readings on paper. Keep it fed with paper, and sneak-click it to tear off the chart.
Close the reactor inside a containment: a room of full blocks with no gaps. Containment Concrete holds 6 bar, Steel Liner 8.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_gene: The secondary loop turns the reactor's heat into rotation. It starts at the steam generator, heated by the primary loop.
Two loops that never mix: the radioactive primary stays around the reactor, while clean water and steam drive the turbine.
A pump draws the steam from the Steam Out port into the turbine's INPUT port...
...where every rotor stage expands it and the Turbine Output turns the shaft.
With an Exhaust Port the turbine stops condensing inside: it lets the spent steam out and makes twice the power from the same steam.
Only a Cooling Tower turns that exhaust back into water. Pump it into a tower port set to INPUT.
This tower, radius 4 and 12 high, condenses 24 mB/t. If the exhaust backs up the turbine stops, so size the tower for its turbines.
The water leaves through a port set to OUTPUT, and a pump sends it back to the steam generator's feedwater port.
Keep the feedwater coming: without it the tubes dry out and stop taking heat, and the reactor loses its heat sink.
Steam left in the generator raises its pressure until it stops taking heat, so the turbine must keep drawing it.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_heat: A pressurized water reactor keeps its coolant liquid under pressure. Fill a fission reactor with Primary Coolant: water and boron from a mixer.
...and the cold leg brings it back, cooled, to the reactor. The flow is whatever the pumps move, and a pressurized core needs plenty.
In the tubes its heat boils the feedwater on the other side into steam. The two never mix.
If a pump stops, the core heats up and boils, the pressure climbs and the relief valve lifts.
A broken pipe drains the loop until the core uncovers and overheats. Primary coolant is radioactive: a leak irradiates.
Stand a Pressurizer on the lid, away from the controller and the rod channels: 2 to 4 Pressurizer or Heater Port blocks under a Relief Valve.
Its steam bubble holds the loop at 155 bar. Heater Ports raise the pressure, on their own or by redstone after a wrench click; spray from the cold leg lowers it.
The Relief Valve lifts at 170 bar and reseats at 160. It can stick open: a redstone signal on it shuts its block valve.
A port set to OUTPUT is the hot leg, one set to INPUT the cold leg. Without a pressurizer they refuse primary coolant.
The Steam Generator is a 3x3 column, 4 to 8 high, of casing around a core of Tube Bundles. More tubes carry more heat.
Its controller goes in a side wall, facing out, with a Tube Bundle right behind it.
Each Steam Generator Port carries one thing, picked with the wrench: primary in, primary out, feedwater in or steam out.
Create pumps drive the loop. The hot leg carries the hot primary coolant from the reactor to the primary inlet...
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_over: A nuclear power plant is a chain of machines joined by pipes and shafts. Here it is whole: each step zooms in on one part and how it joins the next.
The control room runs it all from a distance: link its desks, annunciator and chart recorder to the reactor with the Control Room Linker.
Spent fuel taken out of the reactor goes into the racks at the bottom of the pool, under water, with a Pool Cooler to carry off its heat.
Once it has cooled, move it to Dry Storage Casks or send it to reprocessing.
That is the whole plant, running. The next scenes explain each part in detail.
The reactor and its steam generator stand inside the containment, a sealed room of Containment Concrete with a Containment Door to walk in. From here on it is shown cut away.
In the primary loop a pump carries the hot Primary Coolant from the reactor's OUTPUT port to the steam generator's primary in...
...and a second pump brings it back from primary out to the reactor's INPUT port. The Pressurizer on the lid keeps the loop under pressure.
Pipes may only leave the containment through Containment Penetrations: one for the steam line, one for the feedwater.
The steam line runs from the Steam Out port on top of the steam generator, through its penetration and a pump, into the turbine's INPUT port.
The Turbine Output turns the shaft at the turbine's end: take the rotation from there to your machines.
The turbine's Exhaust Port sends the spent steam, through another pump, to the Cooling Tower's INPUT port.
The tower condenses it into water. From its OUTPUT port a pump sends the water through the other penetration to the steam generator's feedwater port: the loop is closed.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_wast: Fuel leaves the reactor as Hot spent fuel, dated with the day it came out. It goes under water first.
Packages end up in a geological repository, where each one is scored. Depth below the surface counts most: full marks 64 blocks down.
Then the host rock around it, such as deepslate, tuff or basalt, and the waste form: vitrified is best, a raw barrel worst.
Backfill every face with Bentonite, made from clay and borax, or with other packages.
Water within 4 blocks spoils the site: water is what carries waste out.
From a score of 80%% a package is stored: it neither leaks nor irradiates. A Repository Inspector shows the weakest package within 8 blocks.
A Spent Fuel Rack holds nine assemblies on the floor of a pool. Each block of water above cuts its radiation: two stop over 97%%.
Spent fuel cools with time: Warm after about 2 days, Cooled after a week and Aged after 3 weeks. Fresh fuel glows blue.
Its decay heat warms the pool, and a pool too small for its racks boils dry. A Pool Cooler turned from above carries the heat away.
Once Warm or cooler, fuel can move to a Dry Storage Cask. It lets out only 2%% of the radiation and never leaks.
Or reprocess it (PUREX): crush it, dissolve it in nitric acid and centrifuge the solution for uranium and plutonium. Cooled fuel yields more and leaves less waste.
Waste comes in three classes. Low-Level Waste, from scrubbers and contaminated water, is compacted with an iron sheet into a Compacted Waste Drum.
Intermediate-Level Waste is cemented in a mixer, with sand, gravel, an iron sheet and water, into a Cemented Waste Drum.
High-Level Waste from PUREX melts with sand and borax into a Vitrified Waste Canister, in a Vitrification Melter on a lit Blaze Burner.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.radiation_: Fallout leaves the ground contaminated: green dust rises from it, and standing on it irradiates.
A Radiation Scrubber draws it out of the ground of its chunk and the eight around it, the worst first. Drive it from below: it cleans faster up to 256 RPM.
What it absorbs comes out as Low-Level Waste, for a Compacted Waste Drum. Take it out with a funnel or hopper: full, it stops, and the waste inside irradiates.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.reactor_co: The reactor is a multiblock: raise a hollow shell of Reactor Casing.
Leave the casing OPEN above every Control Rod column: rods are moved from up here.
Right-click the controller to form the reactor.
A Mechanical Piston above an open channel raises and lowers the Control Rods.
Super Glue the rods to each other and to the piston head so they move as one.
Withdrawn rods absorb fewer neutrons: the power rises until the hotter fuel and water hold it at a new level.
Inserted rods soak up neutrons: the deeper they sit, the more the reaction is throttled. Fully inserted means shutdown.
The width must be odd (3-9) and the height 4-12.
Inside, raise columns of Fuel Channels: each block holds one fuel assembly.
A central column of Heat Exchangers carries the heat into the coolant.
Control Rods on the corners absorb neutrons: they are the reactor's brakes.
Swap wall casing for a Reactor Fluid Port set to INPUT for coolant...
...and another set to OUTPUT for steam.
A Reactor Fuel Port loads fuel assemblies and ejects spent fuel.
Cap the reactor and place the Reactor Controller at the centre of the top face.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.reactor_mo: Graphite Moderator fills whole interior columns. It slows neutrons, so the Fuel Channels sharing a face with it split more often.
A fuel column with two graphite neighbours is fully moderated; one with a single neighbour, half. A fully moderated core is 35%% more reactive.
Beryllium Reflector belongs in the columns that touch the shell: it bounces escaping neutrons back into the core.
A ring lined all round adds reactivity too. Both make the same fuel more reactive, so leave room for enough Control Rods.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.reactor_re: A Reactor Redstone Port takes the place of a casing block in the shell and puts out a 0-15 signal on its panel side.
Use a Wrench to pick what it reads: temperature, power, fuel, coolant or steam. Like a comparator, any content gives at least 1.
Its last mode is SCRAM. It lights up when SCRAM is pressed on the control panel or the automatic SCRAM trips, and stays on until reset.
Control Rods only move with pistons. Carry the signal to whatever drives them, here a Redstone Link pair and a Gearshift on the piston's shaft.
On SCRAM the Gearshift reverses the piston and the rods go all the way in. Without such wiring, SCRAM only lights the port.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_1: A Radioisotope Generator turns the decay heat of a pellet into a steady 16 RPM on its front shaft. Right-click with a pellet, or feed it by hopper.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_2: Plutonium pellets give 256 stress capacity per RPM and lose half of it every 10 in-game days; waste pellets give 64 and halve every 2. Below a quarter they come out spent.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_3: It irradiates whoever stands near it...
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_4: ...so wall it in. A Block of Depleted Uranium lets only a tenth of the radiation through.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.servo_gear: The Servo Gearbox puts a Mechanical Piston or a Rope Pulley where a redstone signal says. Either end of its shaft takes the rotation; the other end drives.
It finds the actuator through shafts, gearboxes and cogs, and moves it a share of its stroke: no signal keeps it in, a full signal runs it all the way.
Scroll the top or bottom to set the stroke in blocks. It is cut to how far the actuator reaches: a piston's poles, a pulley's rope.
A weaker signal, a shorter move: 8 of 15 of a 3-block stroke is 1.6, so 2 blocks. It always stops on a whole block.
Scroll the other two sides to choose whether a stronger signal extends or retracts.
It stops the actuator exactly on the block and lets it set its blocks down. Every actuator turned at the same speed moves alike; if something blocks the way, it waits and tries again.
A comparator reads where the actuator stands, on the same scale as the signal.
Send it the redstone of a Control Desk dial set to Control rod target, and the rods follow the desk without clutch or gearshift.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tag.contro: Everything to watch and run a plant from one room: screens, consoles, modules, annunciators, recorders and alarms
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tag.nuclea: Everything a nuclear power plant is made of: the reactor and its loops, the turbine hall, the control room, the containment and the spent fuel
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tokamak.te: A tokamak holds a ring of plasma with magnets. Start with a Central Solenoid column, five blocks tall, at its axis.
Keep the coolant flowing. A tokamak without coolant overheats and disrupts, blowing holes in its vessel.
The torus has a 5x5 cross-section. Its floor and roof can hold Breeding Blankets, which turn fusion neutrons into tritium.
Toroidal Field Coils line the walls. The 3x3 core of the ring must stay empty: it is the plasma chamber.
The ring may be 4 to 16 blocks from the solenoid to the plasma. A bigger ring holds more plasma and makes more power.
The Tokamak Controller sits on the outer equator. Right-click it to form the tokamak and open its control panel.
A Fluid Port on INPUT takes water as coolant...
...and one on OUTPUT gives plasma steam for a Plasma Turbine.
The Fuel Injector takes deuterium and tritium, by pipe or by hand with gas cells. On deuterium alone the plasma runs slowly and breeds its first tritium.
Magnet Drives turn rotation into the confining field: one for every 4 blocks of radius, at 64 RPM or more.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tokamak_st: A tokamak does not start by itself. Before its plasma can burn it needs a vacuum, cold magnets, a field and heating.
Burning, a dense and well confined plasma can ignite: turn the heating down and it keeps itself hot.
Vacuum Pumps in the shell empty the plasma chamber: one for every 4 blocks of radius, turning at 128 RPM.
Cryogenic Ports feed the coils liquid helium from a Cryogenic Plant: INPUT takes it in, OUTPUT sends the boiled-off helium back.
Superconducting coils must stay below 20 K. If the helium runs out they warm up and the tokamak shuts down safely.
Neutral Beam Injectors and RF Antennas heat the plasma. Antennas only couple to a dense enough plasma; beams burn a little deuterium.
Heating takes a lot of rotation. Fusion gives back Q times the heating: below a Q of about 3 the plant spends more than it makes.
Press Start in the controller's screen, give it a redstone pulse or throw a desk lever. The screen shows each phase and what is missing.
It pumps down, cools the coils and ramps up the field; then a solenoid pulse breaks a puff of deuterium down into plasma.
Viewports let you watch it: the plasma glows from red to white as it heats, and the windows light up the hall.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.turbine.te: A turbine is a box of casing: 3 to 7 blocks wide and high, and 3 to 16 blocks long.
A column of rotors runs down its axis. Every rotor stage expands 40 mB/t of steam.
Reinforced Turbine Glass can replace casing anywhere on a face, but not on edges or corners.
Fluid Ports go on the faces. One set to INPUT takes the steam...
...and one set to OUTPUT returns the condensed water. Each pair passes 160 mB/t.
The Turbine Output sits at the centre of one end, its shaft pointing out. Right-click it to form the turbine.
Once formed, the rotor spins up while steam flows, and the glass shows how full the turbine is.
Rotors and port pairs both cap the flow; the smaller limit wins. Longer turbines with more ports make more power.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.waste_stor: At the surface a Waste Barrel irradiates whoever comes close, and slowly leaks into the ground around it.
Underground, a repository score decides: depth below the surface, host rock such as deepslate around it, Bentonite backfill on its faces and the waste form. Water within 4 blocks spoils it.

From a score of 80%% a package neither irradiates nor leaks. Raw barrels score lowest: bury them deep in host rock, pack them in Bentonite, or treat the waste first. The old Y=0 rule is a config option.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.weapons_bo: The Nuclear Bomb takes weapons-grade material in its three slots: uranium enriched to 90%% or more, or plutonium, which counts double.
The more it holds, and the richer, the further it wrecks: up to 250 blocks out, round a crater a third as wide.
Power it with redstone: after a ten second countdown it goes off. Sirens in reach sound the attack warning meanwhile.
Its flash burns whoever sees it, a blast wave rolls outwards throwing whoever stands in the open, and fallout drifts downwind.
The Dirty Bomb takes anything radioactive that is not weapons-grade: waste, spent fuel, fragments, RTG pellets.
Its blast is small and leaves no crater, but it scatters its load as fallout, wider the more radioactive the load.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.weapons_mi: A Missile Launch Pad fires a Nuclear Missile at a target far away.
Right-click a block with a Target Designator to aim, then put the designator and a missile in the pad. Sneak-use it in the air for an airburst.
Its three warhead slots take weapons-grade uranium or plutonium for a nuclear warhead, or other radioactive material for a dirty one. Both together salt the fallout.
Power the pad with redstone: after a ten second countdown the missile lifts off and flies to its target.
Air Raid Sirens near the target hear the countdown and sound the attack warning before the missile lands.

jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.accelera: Machines that power the beamline from beside it, with a shaft in their front face, or with Forge Energy from another mod if there is one. A Klystron gives 2 MW of radio-frequency power at 128 RPM; each copper cavity needs 0.25 MW. A Magnet Power Supply feeds 32 magnets at 64 RPM. A Beamline Vacuum Pump keeps 24 beamline blocks at beam vacuum at 64 RPM. Goggles show what each one gives.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.acid_lea: Bulk Acid Leaching: an Encased Fan blowing through sulfuric acid (a placed source or flowing acid) treats the items its air current carries past the acid, on the ground, on belts and on depots, as washing does with water. Acid leaches traces out of rock fines and heavy mineral sand, strips uranium off a loaded adsorbent and washes contamination off waste into Radioactive Sludge. The last catalyst the air passes decides: water then acid leaches, acid then water washes. The spray burns creatures caught in it. Sulfuric acid is mixed from water and gunpowder in a heated basin and is not used up.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.advanced: Works like Create's Redstone Link, but is tuned by a code of four letters or digits instead of two items: click it to type the code. A transmitter sends the strongest redstone signal around it; every receiver with the same code within Create's link range puts it out, into the block it sits on too. Sneak-click it with an empty hand to switch between transmitting and receiving. Control modules can send on a code as well: choose the Advanced Redstone Link output and type the code in their setup screen. Looking at it shows its code and signal on the right of the screen.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.annuncia: Six alarm windows over an ACK and a RESET button. Click a window with a Control Room Linker to link it to a reactor, turbine, steam generator, containment or any other machine (click the frame to link all six), and wrench a window to choose its alarm, threshold and label. A tripped window flashes and the horn sounds until you press ACK; it then stays lit while the condition lasts, flashes slowly once it clears and goes dark on RESET. The first window to trip is marked as the first out. Redstone pulses into its left and right sides (seen from the front) press ACK and RESET; the back and bottom give a signal while an alarm waits for ACK, and a comparator reads how many windows are lit.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.beam_dum: Where a beamline ends when there is nothing to hit. It takes the whole beam and gives off radiation while it does; it also becomes radioactive itself, and keeps radiating after the beam stops, fading with time. Breaking an activated dump leaves radioactive waste and contaminates the ground: let it cool first. Shield it with concrete or lead.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.beamline: Beamline blocks run along the beam: place them looking along the line, or turn them with a wrench. Each RF Cavity adds 2.5 MeV with full radio-frequency power. Without a Quadrupole Magnet every four blocks the beam spreads and is lost: half the quadrupoles keep only a quarter of it. A Bending Magnet sends the beam to the side it faces. Beam Pipes have windows to watch the beam; a Beam Position Monitor gives a comparator signal with the beam current.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.blast_do: A sliding door that survives nuclear blasts. Fill a 2x2 to 4x4 opening with Steel or Lead Blast Door leaves and ring it with Blast Door Frame, with a Blast Door Controller as one of the frame blocks; the controller's shaft runs through the wall, across the door. Turning the shaft one way opens the door and the other way shuts it, faster at higher speed; without rotation, a rising redstone signal opens it and a falling one shuts it. The panel slides towards the controller when it sits beside the door. Shut leaves shrug off explosions, count as containment wall and stop radiation: lead lets 2% through, steel 15%. A comparator reads how far open the door is.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.chart_re: Draws up to three readings of a linked machine on a strip of paper. Link it with a Control Room Linker like a monitor, give it paper by hand or with a hopper, and wrench it to choose what each pen draws and how fast the paper runs (a sample every 1, 5 or 20 ticks). One sheet lasts 240 samples; without paper the chart stops, and a comparator reads how much is left. Click it to see the paper left; sneak-click empty-handed to tear the chart off as a Chart Roll, which you can use anywhere to read it.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.containm: Build a sealed building around the reactor and place a Containment Monitor anywhere inside: it measures the air enclosed (up to 32768 blocks) and keeps the steam, hydrogen and radioactivity of an accident in instead of letting them out. Gas leaks through anything that is not a full block, such as doors, slabs and pipes. Every wall block holds a pressure: Containment Concrete 6 bar, Steel Liner 8, ordinary blocks 1.5; above the weakest one the building bursts there. Pipes go through Containment Penetrations, which pass fluid along their axis. Passive Autocatalytic Recombiners set in the wall remove hydrogen before it burns (4% can ignite, 8% always does); a Filtered Vent in the wall opens with redstone and bleeds the overpressure out, keeping 99% of the radioactivity. Click the monitor to measure again or to clear a repaired burst; comparators read the pressure against what the weakest wall holds.

A two-block-high steel door for the containment wall. Shut, it seals like the wall around it and holds 8 bar; open, the doorway is a hole in the containment. Click it or power it with redstone: it pulls out of its frame and slides sideways along the wall. Two side by side, hinged on opposite sides, open as a pair. While the containment behind it is more than 0.2 bar above the outside it stays pressure-locked and will not open.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.contamin: Heavy fallout turns the surface of lakes and rivers into Contaminated Water. It irradiates; a centrifuge separates it into clean water and low-level waste.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.control_: Control Desks placed side by side, or meeting at a corner, join into one console; link any of them with the Control Room Linker to link the whole console. Each straight desk holds four control modules and each corner two, one on each arm (high up on an inner corner, low down on an outer one): click a slot with a module to fit it, wrench the module to choose what it does and where its redstone goes, sneak-wrench to take it out, and click it with an empty hand to work it (sneak to turn a dial down). Push buttons SCRAM and reset the reactor, send a pulse or start and shut down a tokamak; levers switch the automatic SCRAM, a tokamak's start, shutdown or heating or a redstone output; dials set the rod target, the SCRAM threshold or a redstone level; lamps light on SCRAM, running, no signal or an alarm; gauges show any reading, LED displays show it in digits, bar graphs as a column of lights and trend recorders as a line over the last minutes; core maps and plasma sections picture a reactor's core or a tokamak's plasma, and a guarded button keeps a SCRAM under a cover. Any module can put its state out as redstone below the desk or on a Create Redstone Link frequency.

Right-click a Monitor with a wrench to set up its screen, from any of its blocks: a title of your own, the layout (readings, graph, both, or the automatic one that switches on click), its style (the standard screen, a process computer's CRT page or a mimic board's panel), what the graph's lines plot (two always, a third when you choose one; each on its own scale), and which readings it lists in which order. Click a reading in the list to show or hide it or move it up or down. A screen that grows keeps its setup.

Stacked in columns inside a reactor, Control Rods soak up neutrons: the deeper they sit in the core, the more they hold back the chain reaction, and fully inserted they shut it down. They only move with a Mechanical Piston above an open column of the lid, glued to each other and to the piston head. Wire the reactor's SCRAM signal to the piston to drive them in when it trips.

Build a control room. Click a reactor, turbine or cooling tower (any of their blocks) with the Control Room Linker, or any other block to watch the radiation there, then click a Monitor, Control Desk or Nuclear Alarm to link it; sneak-click a device to unlink it. Monitors side by side join into one screen up to 8x8 that shows the readings and two minutes of history; click it to change page. Control Desks carry modules that SCRAM the reactor, switch its automatic SCRAM and set a rod target: Redstone Ports in Insert rods or Withdraw rods mode light up until the rods reach it, to drive the clutch and gearshift of the pistons. The alarm rings and powers every side past the threshold set on its sides, for the reading chosen on its top. Devices reach 128 blocks.

A flat-topped console for four control modules in two rows, its top level with the rail of a Control Desk. Tables side by side join into one, and tables, desks and wall panels touching side by side share one console and its link. Fit, set up and work modules as on a desk.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.controll: A Control Desk module that runs the reactor on its own. Fit it in a desk linked to a fission reactor and wrench it to choose Automatic power (setpoint in MW), Automatic temperature (in °C) or, on a reactor with a pressurizer, Automatic pressure (in bar, through the heaters and the spray), and to switch it between automatic and standby. Click it to raise the setpoint and sneak-click to lower it. In power and temperature mode it sets the reactor's rod target like a PID controller; Redstone Ports in Insert rods or Withdraw rods mode still have to drive the rod pistons. It lets go during a SCRAM or while the core is not formed, and picks up smoothly again afterwards. Tune it under controlRoom.pid in the config.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.cooling_: A hyperboloid of Cooling Tower Casing that turns steam or turbine exhaust back into water (heavy into heavy water). A turbine with an Exhaust Port sends its spent steam here and makes twice the power. Base radius 4 to 16, on a full floor; the walls narrow to a waist and flare out at the open top. It condenses half its base radius times its height in mB/t, and Fans in the bottom wall layers add up to double that. Ports go in the floor or the two wall layers above it; the controller sits in the bottom wall layer facing out. See its Ponder scene.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.corium: When an overheated core melts, its fuel turns into Corium: molten core that falls through open space and melts its way down through blocks until its heat runs out, then freezes into Solidified Corium, which stays fiercely radioactive and slowly contaminates its chunk. Corium meeting water sets off a steam explosion, and melting concrete inside a containment gives off more hydrogen. It cannot melt bedrock or very blast-resistant blocks, and on a Core Catcher floor under the reactor it spreads out and freezes fast. Before that, cladding hotter than 1200 °C reacts with steam and makes hydrogen, and a pressurized vessel kept above 250 bar breaks. Setting pwr.accidents.legacyMeltdown in the config brings back the old meltdown: one big explosion and wide fallout.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.cryoplan: The Cryogenic Plant liquefies the helium that keeps a tokamak's coils superconducting. Build a 3x3 block of Cryogenic Plant Casing 3 to 5 high, with the controller in the middle of a side wall facing out, at least one Helium Compressor in the walls with its shaft side facing out, and Cryogenic Plant Ports (the wrench sets what each one carries). Warm helium goes in through a Warm helium in port and leaves a Liquid helium out port as liquid: 2 mB/t per layer of height at 128 RPM, less when slower and nothing below 32 RPM. The plant loads the network with 10240 SU/RPM per layer, shared among its compressors. About 1% of the helium leaks out on every pass. Liquid nitrogen fed through a nitrogen port pre-cools it for 50% more output, boiling off 1 mB of nitrogen per mB of liquid helium. A plant with a Liquid Air port liquefies air instead, 5 mB/t per layer: centrifuge the liquid air into liquid nitrogen and the helium for a first charge.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.decontam: Acid leaching decontaminates: low-level waste, spent D-T pellets and depleted RTG pellets come out as clean iron nuggets, and their activity as Radioactive Sludge. An Item Drain pours the sludge out as contaminated water, which a centrifuge cleans into water and a little low-level waste.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.depleted: Depleted uranium (under 0.7%) is dense: a block of it lets only 10% of radiation through, the best shield there is. Its heavy plate armour protects better than diamond and, as a full set, stops 98% of radiation, but slows you by about a sixth. A crusher turns the block back into metal.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.dirty_bo: A radiological weapon. Load it with anything radioactive that is not weapons-grade (waste, spent fuel, fragments, RTG pellets) and power it with redstone: after 10 seconds a small blast scatters the load. No crater, but the more radioactive the load, the wider the fallout (up to 128 blocks) and the hotter the spot left at ground zero. A launch pad also takes radioactive material: on its own it makes a dirty warhead, packed with fissile material it salts a nuclear one for dirtier fallout.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.fusion_t: The fusion turbine is built like the steam turbine, from these blocks, around a Plasma Turbine at the centre of one end: a box 3-7 blocks wide and high and 3-16 long, with a column of Fusion Turbine Rotors on its axis and a pair of Fusion Turbine Fluid Ports, one on input and one on output, for every 80 mB/t of plasma steam. Each rotor expands 20 mB/t.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.guarded_: A push button under a hinged cover, so a SCRAM or a tokamak shutdown is never pressed by mistake. The first click lifts the cover, the next presses the button; a sneaking click closes it, and it falls shut by itself after five seconds.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.heavy_mi: Washing sand, red sand or gravel sometimes pans out heavy mineral sand (monazite and zircon). Acid leaching it is the only source of thorium dioxide, with a chance of uranium concentrate and of beryllium. Thorium is fertile, not fissile: it becomes fuel when seeded and burnt in a reactor, or irradiated by a fan.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.helium_w: The Helium Well is the first step towards liquid helium. Turned by a shaft through its back, it draws traces of helium gas out of the rock: 0.02 mB/t (24 mB a minute) at 128 RPM, less when slower and nothing below 32 RPM, for 1024 SU/RPM. It keeps up to 1000 mB and pushes the gas into tanks and machines on any other side, or pipes can drain it; when full it stops. Feed the helium gas to a Cryogenic Plant's Warm helium in port and it comes out as liquid helium, which Spouts can put in gas cells.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.irradiat: Bulk Irradiation: an Encased Fan blowing past an Irradiation Source (a capsule of waste in an open cage, crafted from Radioactive Waste) bathes the items in its air current in neutrons. Air passes through the source's cage; a full block would stop the current, so ordinary radioactive blocks do not work. Thorium dioxide becomes irradiated thorium, which dissolves in nitric acid into a little uranium-233 dioxide and thorium back. Depleted uranium (oxide or metal) becomes irradiated depleted uranium, which dissolves in nitric acid into uranyl nitrate and a trace of spent fuel solution for plutonium. The green current doses creatures caught in it.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.led_disp: Shows a reading of the linked machine in digits, with its unit. LED displays side by side in a row of a desk, table or wall panel join into one wider display, across joined blocks of the same kind too (up to eight modules): the wider it is, the more digits and a label on top. The leftmost module sets the whole display; wrench any of its modules to choose the reading and the label. Too big a value reads OL; a reading the machine does not have reads dashes.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.medicine: Potassium Iodide (dried kelp and bone meal, mixed hot in water) halves the radiation you take up for 3 minutes: take it before going near a hot core. Prussian Blue (iron nuggets and blue dye in sulfuric acid) flushes 15 rad of dose a second for 30 seconds, curing radiation sickness. Neither lowers the lifetime total. Both are eaten whatever your hunger, then wait 5 seconds.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.missile_: The Missile Launch Pad fires a Nuclear Missile at a block far away. Right-click the target with a Target Designator, then put the designator, a missile and the warhead in the pad. Its three warhead slots take weapons-grade uranium or plutonium for a nuclear warhead, or other radioactive material for a dirty one; both together make a salted warhead with dirtier, wider fallout. Power the pad with redstone: after a 10 second countdown the missile lifts off. The missile and the warhead are used up; the designator stays. Sneak-use the designator in the air to set an airburst: the missile goes off high above its target, digs no crater and leaves a tenth of the fallout, but its blast and flash reach further. Sirens near the target sound the attack warning while it flies.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.moderati: Graphite Moderator and Beryllium Reflector fill whole interior columns of a fission reactor, like Fuel Channels. Graphite slows neutrons so the fuel beside it splits more: a Fuel Channel with two graphite columns sharing a face with it is fully moderated, and a fully moderated core gains about 1500 pcm of reactivity, but graphite keeps moderating when the water boils, so steam in its core adds reactivity instead of taking it away. Beryllium lining the columns that touch the shell bounces escaping neutrons back: a complete ring adds about 1000 pcm. Both make the same fuel more reactive, so they also need more control rods.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.mox: MOX fuel mixes plutonium dioxide into depleted uranium dioxide. In a reactor it burns like 12% uranium, a little more reactive and hotter, and control rods hold it back less, so it needs more of them. Spent MOX is reprocessed like spent fuel but gives back less plutonium than went in.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.neutral_: Auxiliary heating for a tokamak. Build it into the shell in place of a casing block, facing out, and turn the shaft on its outer face: at 128 RPM it fires 20 MW of fast deuterium atoms into the plasma, nothing at 32 RPM or less and in proportion in between. It is very heavy, 32768 SU per RPM, so a megawatt of beam costs more than the plasma turbine makes from a megawatt of fusion: run it to heat the plasma up and ease it off once it burns. The beams take 0.02 mB/t of deuterium per MW from the tokamak and lose power when the tank runs low. They heat at any plasma density. Goggles show its power and the plasma.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.nuclear_: What a nuclear crater leaves. Trinitite is the sand and rock of the crater's floor fused into green glass by the fireball, among basalt, obsidian and, at the very centre, magma; it is faintly radioactive. Charred Logs are what the flash leaves of trees within its reach.

A nuclear weapon. Its three slots take weapons-grade material: uranium enriched to 90% or more, or plutonium, which counts double. The more it holds and the richer it is, the more powerful the blast: it wrecks what stands up to 250 blocks from ground zero and digs a crater about a third as wide, with a raised rim and a floor of glassy trinitite. Power it with redstone and it goes off after a 10 second countdown; taking the signal away stops the countdown. Its flash burns whoever sees the fireball and scorches the land further out still, prompt radiation doses whoever is near, a blast wave hurts and throws whoever is in the open, and fallout drifts downwind. Blast doors and bedrock survive it. Sirens within reach sound the attack warning during the countdown.

A big cannon shell from Create Big Cannons with a nuclear warhead: craft a high explosive shell with a Nuclear Bomb and one to four weapons-grade cores. Four cores are a fully loaded Nuclear Bomb; fewer, a smaller blast. Load and fire it like any other shell; its fuze sets it off, and set off high enough above the ground it is an airburst.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.particle: A particle accelerator starts at its controller. Put an Ion Source right in front of it, shaft across the beam, and fill it with hydrogen (electrolyse brine). From the source a beamline runs on: Beam Pipes, RF Cavities that add energy, Quadrupole Magnets that keep the beam focused (one per four blocks), Bending Magnets to turn it and Beam Position Monitors to read it, until it ends in a Beam Dump or a target. Klystrons, Magnet Power Supplies and Vacuum Pumps beside the line power it. Right-click the controller to check the structure and open its panel; a redstone signal starts the beam and taking it away stops it. A longer linac with more cavities reaches higher energies.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.pressuri: Turns a fission reactor into a pressurized water reactor. Stack 2 to 4 Pressurizer or Pressurizer Heater Port blocks on the reactor's lid, anywhere but over the controller or a control rod channel, cap them with a Relief Valve and fill the reactor with Primary Coolant (boron mixed into water) instead of water. The coolant then carries the heat out without boiling: Mechanical Pumps must move the Hot Primary Coolant from an output port to a Steam Generator and the cooled coolant back into an input port; with every pump stopped only a trickle circulates. Heater ports hold 155 bar on their own; wrench one for manual mode, where it heats only while powered by redstone. The valve opens at 170 bar and can stick open: a redstone signal on it shuts it off. A comparator reads 15 from it while it is open.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.radiatio: Enriched uranium, spent fuel and radioactive waste irradiate whoever carries them. A Geiger counter shows the dose; a full hazmat suit stops 95% of it.

Draws ground contamination out of its chunk and the chunks around it, the worst first. Drive it with a shaft from below; it cleans faster up to 256 RPM. What it absorbs comes out as Low-Level Waste for a funnel or hopper; when full it stops. Contamination comes from fallout, meltdowns and waste stored outside a proper repository.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.reactor_: Part of a fission reactor's shell, for its coolant. On INPUT it takes water, or Primary Coolant in a pressurized plant; on OUTPUT it gives the steam, or the hot primary coolant, the core heats. A reactor needs at least one of each. Wrench it to switch the mode, sneak-wrench to turn its face.

Fuel assemblies are pressed from uranium dioxide pellets. Each Fuel Channel in a reactor holds one assembly. Richer fuel lasts longer and is more reactive. Each fuel rod block is rated 50 MW of heat, and the reactor's power is shown as a share of that rating; spent fuel keeps its enrichment and can be reprocessed for plutonium.

Part of a fission reactor's shell. On INPUT it takes fuel assemblies, by hand, hopper, funnel or chute, and loads them into the free Fuel Channels; on OUTPUT it hands out the spent fuel the channels eject. Wrench it to switch the mode, sneak-wrench to turn its face.

A running core makes iodine, which decays into xenon, a neutron poison. At steady power it holds the reactor back a little; after power drops it keeps building for a few minutes before it decays, so a reactor just shut down needs more rods out to restart. Fission products also keep heating the core after a SCRAM, about 7% of the fission heat, fading over a few minutes: keep the coolant flowing. The control panel, the panel that shows while looking at the controller and Display Links show reactivity, xenon and decay heat.

Part of a reactor's shell. It puts out a 0-15 signal on its panel side: temperature, power, fuel, coolant or steam, or the SCRAM signal, which turns on when SCRAM is pressed or the automatic SCRAM trips. Control rods only move with pistons, so wire the SCRAM signal to them. Wrench to change the mode, sneak-wrench to turn it.

Part of a fission reactor's shell. It gives a redstone signal on the face it points at, rising with the core temperature: 0 at 20 °C up to 15 at 3500 °C. Wrench it to turn its face. Goggles show the exact temperature, and a Display Link reads it too.

A lead glass window that takes the place of a Reactor Casing block in a fission reactor's walls. Through it you watch the fuel channels: how much fuel they hold, how brightly they glow with the power, and whether coolant flows past them. Viewports side by side join into one pane.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.reproces: Spent fuel is reprocessed for plutonium: crush it into fragments, dissolve them in nitric acid in a heated mixer (uranium comes back as uranyl nitrate one tier lower), separate the solution in a centrifuge into plutonium nitrate, recovered acid and high-level waste, then make plutonium dioxide and reduce it to metal. Leaner fuel breeds more plutonium. Plutonium is far more radioactive than uranium and burns whoever carries it without a hazmat suit.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.rf_anten: Radio-frequency heating for a tokamak: a shell block with a shaft on its outer face, like the Neutral Beam Injector. At 64 RPM it sends 12 MW into the plasma (nothing at 16 RPM or less) for 13312 SU per RPM and no fuel, but the waves only couple to a plasma denser than about 15% of its density limit, fully above about 35%: start the plasma with the solenoid and the beams, then let the antennas carry it. Goggles warn when the plasma is too thin.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.rock_fin: Crushing granite, tuff, deepslate or cobbled deepslate gives fines with the rock's usual by-products. Acid leaching the fines washes out traces: granite gives uranium concentrate and sometimes thorium dioxide, tuff spodumene concentrate, deepslate uranium concentrate and fluorite. Rock is everywhere, so this never runs out, but each unit costs between one and two times what the same unit costs from ore.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.rtg: A small generator that turns decay heat into a steady 16 RPM, with no fuel to pump. Load it with RTG pellets by hand or by hopper: plutonium pellets give 256 stress capacity per RPM and halve in strength every 10 in-game days, waste pellets 64 and every 2 days. Below a quarter of their charge they come out spent. It irradiates its surroundings; wall it in with depleted uranium.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.screen_m: Screens for a desk, table or wall panel. The Bar Graph shows a reading as a column of LEDs, green, then amber, then red from the level set in its screen. The Trend Recorder draws a reading over its last 48 samples, taken every 1, 5 or 20 seconds. The Core Map shows a fission reactor from above, north at the top: fuel green to red as it burns, control channels filling blue as their rods go in. The Plasma Section shows a cut through a tokamak with its plasma, glowing with its temperature and shaking as it grows unstable. Four Core Maps or four Plasma Sections filling one block make one big screen; wrench any of them to set it up.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.seawater: Water boiled down in a heated basin becomes brine (4:1). A centrifuge spins brine into lithium carbonate, borax and fresh water. String and bone meal mixed with water make an amidoxime adsorbent, which picks up the uranium of sea water when mixed with water or, faster, with a little brine; acid leaching the loaded adsorbent gives uranium concentrate and returns half of the adsorbent.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.seismic_: Feels every nuclear and dirty bomb detonation in its dimension and remembers the last eight: power, distance, bearing and how long ago. Read it with goggles (sneak to see them all) or a Display Link. A comparator follows the strongest detonation of the last five minutes, weaker the farther away it went off.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.servo_ge: Puts a Mechanical Piston or Rope Pulley where a redstone signal says. Turn either end of its shaft; the other end drives the actuators beyond it, through shafts, gearboxes or cogs. The signal sets a share of the stroke: 0 keeps it retracted, 15 runs it the whole stroke, 8 a little over half, rounded to whole blocks. Scroll one pair of its sides to set the stroke in blocks (cut to the piston's poles or the pulley's rope) and the other to choose whether a stronger signal extends or retracts. It stops the actuator exactly on the block and lets it set its blocks down; every actuator turned at the same speed moves alike. A comparator reads where the nearest one stands, on the signal's scale. Send it the redstone of a Control Desk dial set to Control rod target, which puts the target out as 0-15, and the rods follow the desk.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.shelter: Place it inside a closed room to make a fallout shelter; its shaft can come in through the wall. It surveys the room: up to 4096 blocks of air, with every block of the walls, floor and ceiling solid and at least as blast resistant as concrete (no glass or wool). A certified shelter lets in only 10% of a blast wave's overpressure, and while the unit turns at 16 RPM or more it filters out 95% of the dose from fallout and contaminated ground. Goggles show what is missing.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.sirens: The Air Raid Siren sounds a steady alert while it gets a redstone signal, and on its own the faster attack warning when a missile, bomb or launch countdown is aimed within 96 blocks of it, plus the reach of the threat's fallout. The Hand-Crank Siren needs no power: it sounds while its shaft from below turns at 32 RPM or more, higher pitched the faster it turns. Both can be heard 128 blocks away, and a comparator reads 15 from them while they sound.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.spent_fu: Spent fuel leaves the core Hot and cools as its short-lived fission products decay: Hot for about two in-game days, then Warm, Cooled after about a week and Aged after about three weeks. The tooltip shows the grade. Hot fuel is the most radioactive and burns bare hands; cooler fuel crushes into more fragments and less waste, so each grade has its own crushing recipe. Put fresh assemblies in Spent Fuel Racks at the bottom of a water pool: every block of water straight above a rack cuts its radiation, and two or more make it safe. The pool must also carry the decay heat away (0.4 kW per water block, up to 20 kW per fresh assembly) or it boils off a layer at a time; Pool Coolers in the water, turned by a shaft from above, add up to 60 kW each at 64 RPM. Fuel that is Warm or cooler can go into a Dry Cask, which lets almost nothing out. Both hold nine assemblies: click with fuel to load, empty-handed to take one out. Hoppers work and comparators read how full they are.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.steam_ge: Boils feedwater with the heat of a pressurized reactor's primary coolant. A 3x3 column 4 to 8 blocks tall: full layers of casing on top and bottom, and in the layers between, a column of Tube Bundles in the middle walled in by Casing, Ports and the Controller, which faces out with a tube bundle right behind it. Wrench each Port to set what it carries: Primary in (hot coolant from the reactor), Primary out (cooled coolant back to the reactor), Feedwater in (water) and Steam out (to the turbines); it needs one of each. More tube bundles move more heat. If the feedwater runs out the tubes dry up and stop cooling the reactor.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.thorium_: Thorium fuel: three thorium dioxide and one fissile seed (low-enriched uranium dioxide or uranium-233 dioxide) compact into four pellets, assembled into fuel like uranium. In the reactor it starts weak, only the seed fissions, and grows more reactive as the thorium breeds uranium-233, peaking about half way; it lasts 40% longer than low-enriched uranium. Spent thorium fuel cools in pools and casks like the others; crush it, dissolve the fragments in nitric acid, and centrifuge the solution into uranium-233 nitrate, recovered acid, thorium dioxide and high-level waste. Denitrated, the uranium-233 seeds new pellets.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.tokamak: A ring-shaped fusion reactor around a Central Solenoid. Feed it deuterium and tritium, water as coolant, rotation for its Magnet Drives, vacuum pumps and liquid helium for its coils, then press Start: it pumps down, cools its coils, ramps the field, lights the plasma and heats it to a burn, making plasma steam for a Plasma Turbine. See its Ponder scene.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.tokamak_: Tokamak Cryogenic Ports go in the tokamak shell. In input mode they take liquid helium in to cool the superconducting coils; in output mode they give back the warm helium gas the coils boil off, for a cryogenic plant to liquefy again. The wrench toggles the mode. They connect to pipes, and also push or pull on their own with a tank or Cryogenic Plant Port right next to them, so the plant can stand against the shell. A tokamak cannot start until liquid helium has cooled its coils.

Part of a tokamak's shell. On INPUT it takes water as coolant; on OUTPUT it gives the plasma steam a burning plasma boils it into, for a Plasma Turbine. Keep the coolant flowing: a tokamak without it overheats and disrupts.

Part of a tokamak's shell that fuels the plasma with deuterium and tritium, by pipe or by hand with gas cells. On deuterium alone the plasma burns slowly and breeds its first tritium in the blankets. Switched to OUTPUT it hands out the bred tritium above the reserve the tokamak keeps.

Part of a tokamak's shell that turns rotation into the field that confines the plasma. A tokamak needs one for every 4 blocks of radius, turning at 64 RPM or more. Short of drives or speed, the field is weaker and holds the plasma less well.

The blocks a tokamak's shell is made of. The torus has a 5x5 cross-section around an empty 3x3 plasma chamber, 4 to 16 blocks from the Central Solenoid, a column five blocks tall at its axis. Toroidal Field Coils line its walls, Breeding Blankets in its floor and roof turn fusion neutrons into tritium, and the rest is plain shell: Tokamak Vacuum Vessel or Cryostat Casing, which count the same. See the tokamak's Ponder scene.

The Tokamak Vacuum Pump goes in the tokamak shell with its shaft side facing out, and holds the vacuum the plasma needs. One pump at 128 RPM (2048 SU/RPM) is enough for a tokamak of major radius 4; every 4 blocks more of radius needs another. Slower pumps count for less, and below 32 RPM they do not pump at all. Goggles show the chamber pressure.

A quartz window for the tokamak shell: it seals the chamber like a casing block and lets you watch the plasma inside. It is the hall's light while the plasma burns: dark when there is none, a dim glow at breakdown and brighter as the plasma heats up. Several viewports side by side make one big window.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.turbine: A box multiblock 3-7 blocks wide and high and 3-16 long, with a rotor column on its axis and this block at the centre of one end. Each rotor expands 40 mB/t of steam (20 of plasma steam); each input/output port pair passes 160 (80). Reinforced Turbine Glass shows the rotor and steam inside.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.turbine_: Goes on a turbine's face like a fluid port. A turbine with one stops condensing its steam inside: it lets it out here as exhaust steam and makes twice the power from the same steam. Only a Cooling Tower turns exhaust steam back into water; if it backs up, the turbine stops. Works on steam and plasma turbines.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.vitrific: Melts high-level waste with sand and borax into a Vitrified Waste Canister. It has no heater of its own: like a basin, it sits on a Blaze Burner that must be lit, and a superheated burner melts twice as fast. Click it with ingredients or feed it with funnels and hoppers; each kind of ingredient gets its own slot. Click it empty-handed to take the canisters out, or sneak to take an ingredient back. The waste inside irradiates through its walls.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.wall_con: A plate for four control modules, hung on the side of a solid block. Panels side by side join into one, and panels on the same wall, side by side or one above another, make one console with any desk or table beside them. A gauge on a wall panel shows its dial face on. Break the wall and the panel falls off with its modules.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.waste_cl: Radioactive waste comes in three classes, each with its own treatment. Low-Level Waste (from contaminated water and radiation scrubbers) is compacted with an iron sheet by a Mechanical Press over a basin into a Compacted Waste Drum. Intermediate-Level Waste (from crushing spent fuel and spent pellets) is mixed with sand, gravel, water and an iron sheet into a Cemented Waste Drum. High-Level Waste (the fission products from reprocessing) is fierce and warm: melt it with sand and borax in a Vitrification Melter into a Vitrified Waste Canister. Treated packages leak less and store better in a repository.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.info.waste_st: A placed waste package (barrel, drum or canister) irradiates whoever comes close and slowly leaks into the ground of its chunk unless it sits in a good geological repository. Its score adds up four barriers: depth below the surface (full at 64 blocks), host rock such as deepslate, tuff or basalt within 3 blocks, backfill covering its faces (Bentonite or other packages) and the waste form (a raw barrel counts least, a vitrified canister most). A fluid source within 4 blocks takes a large share off. From 80% it counts as stored and neither irradiates nor leaks; below that it does less the higher the score. A Repository Inspector shows the packages within 8 blocks and what the weakest one lacks, by goggles, Display Link or comparator. waste.repository.legacyDepthRule in the config brings back the old rule: stored at Y=0 or lower. See its Ponder scene.
jei.create_nuclearindustry.processing_ti: %ss at %s RPM, faster when spun faster
jei.create_nuclearindustry.vitrification: Optional: a superheated Blaze Burner melts twice as fast
